skills.name: Dicotyledons: the bean plant, and differences from monocotyledons

sections.heading: The bean plant
Monocots and dicots compared
sections.text:
• Seed leaves: one (monocot) vs two (dicot).
• Leaf veins: parallel vs net.
• Leaf shape: often long and narrow vs broad.
• Roots: fibrous vs taproot.
• Flower parts: in threes vs in fours or fives.
• Vascular bundles in the stem: scattered vs in a ring.
Maize, rice and palm are monocots; beans, mango and cocoa are dicots.

sections.heading: Why it matters on the farm
sections.text:
Knowing the group helps farmers. Legumes (beans, groundnuts, soya) are dicots whose nodules add nitrogen to the soil, so they are rotated or intercropped with maize.
Some weedkillers kill broad-leaved dicot weeds but not monocot grasses like maize: knowing the difference avoids killing the crop.

key_words.meaning: one main root with side roots
a plant of the bean family with nitrogen-fixing nodules

examples: Maize: monocot, fibrous roots, parallel veins

mistake.wrong: Maize has net veins like beans
mistake.why: Parallel veins are a monocot feature; maize is a monocot.

worked_example.problem: A plant has broad leaves with net veins, a taproot and flowers with five petals. Is it a monocot or a dicot?

cards.idea: Each part of the bean plant has a job.
Dicots have net veins and taproots; monocots parallel veins and fibrous roots.
example: Bean: net veins. Maize: parallel veins.

cards.idea: Dicot flower parts are in fours or fives; monocot parts in threes.

pick.q: Long narrow leaves with parallel veins and fibrous roots
e: Dicots have net veins and taproots.
Ferns do not have these features.
pick.y: Parallel veins and fibrous roots: monocot.

pick.q: A flower with 5 petals and leaves with a network of veins
e: Monocot flowers are in threes, with parallel veins.
pick.y: Five petals and net veins: dicot.

pick.q: A stem with vascular bundles scattered all through it
e: Dicot bundles are in a ring.
Conifers have bundles in a ring.

pick.r: anchoring the plant and absorbing water and minerals
e: Leaves are the main site of gas exchange.
pick.y: Roots hold the plant and take in water.
The bacteria make nitrogen compounds for the plant.

pick.r: protecting the seeds and helping to disperse them
e: Leaves are the main photosynthetic organs.
pick.y: The pod is the fruit; it splits to release seeds.

questions.prompt: What is the main function of this part of a bean plant? {X.q}

pick.q: What kind of veins does a dicot leaf have?
e: Veins run through the whole leaf.

pick.q: What kind of root system does maize have?
pick.y: Monocots have many similar fibrous roots.

pick.q: In which plants are the flower parts usually in threes?
e: Dicot flowers have parts in fours or fives.
pick.y: Lilies and onions: parts in threes.

pick.q: Long narrow leaves with parallel veins and fibrous roots
e: Dicots have net veins and taproots.
Ferns do not have these features.
pick.y: Parallel veins and fibrous roots: monocot.

pick.q: A flower with 5 petals and leaves with a network of veins
e: Monocot flowers are in threes, with parallel veins.
pick.y: Five petals and net veins: dicot.

pick.q: A stem with vascular bundles scattered all through it
e: Dicot bundles are in a ring.
Conifers have bundles in a ring.

pick.q: Why do farmers often plant beans or groundnuts between rows of maize?
pick.r: Their root nodules add nitrogen to the soil
w: They make the maize grow faster by photosynthesis
e: Shading is a small benefit, not the main one.
They do not photosynthesise for maize.
They do not repel all insects.

pick.q: Which pair shows one monocot feature and one dicot feature?
w: parts in threes (dicot); parts in fives (monocot)
e: Net veins are dicot; fibrous roots are monocot.
Monocots have one cotyledon; dicots two.
Threes are monocot; fives are dicot.
pick.y: Match each feature to its group.

pick.q: A seed splits easily into two halves. What does this tell you?
pick.r: It is a dicot seed with two cotyledons
e: The embryo lies between the halves.
pick.y: The two halves are the two cotyledons.
